extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for computing reply periods, consequences of failing to reply, shortened statutory periods, specified time limits, and extensions of time during U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP §710 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to prosecute (35 U.S.C. 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon failure of the applicant to prosecute the application within six months after any action therein, of which notice has been given or mailed to the applicant, or within such shorter time, not less than thirty days, as fixed by the Director in such action, the application shall be regarded as abandoned ... unless it be shown to the satisfaction of the Director that such delay was unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maximum statutory period for reply is 6 months (35 U.S.C. 133). Shortened periods (but not less than 30 days) are commonly used. Abandonment occurs after midnight of the date the period expired; holidays/weekends do not change abandonment date. A petition to revive may be available under 37 CFR 1.137 for unavoidable or unintentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for Government applications (35 U.S.C. 267)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may extend the time for taking any action to three years, when an application has become the property of the United States and the head of the appropriate department or agency ... has certified ... that the invention disclosed therein is important to the armament or defense of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension under 35 U.S.C. 267 is decided by the Technology Center Director of the relevant work group (example: work group 3640).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.135 — Abandonment for failure to reply within time period
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If an applicant ... fails to reply within the time period provided under § 1.134 and § 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise. (b) Prosecution to save must include such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require. (c) When reply is a bona fide attempt ... but an inadvertent omission exists, applicant may be given a new time period under § 1.134 to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission of, or refusal to admit, any amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment. Examiners may accept a bona fide but incomplete reply as adequate to avoid abandonment and provide a shortened statutory time to correct inadvertent omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission — 1-month shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: When reply by the applicant is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and is substantially a complete reply to the non-final Office action, but consideration of some matter or compliance with some requirement has been inadvertently omitted, applicant may be given a new time period for reply under § 1.134 to supply the omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may set a 1-month (not less than 30 days) shortened statutory period to correct inadvertent omissions (e.g., unsigned amendment, missing duplicate paper, additional claims fees). Examiner discretion applies: if omission was not inadvertent or applicant is abusing the provision to gain time, the examiner should require the omission be supplied within the original reply period (including available extensions). See MPEP §714.03 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual time for reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action to the date of receipt by the Office of applicant’s reply. No cognizance is taken of fractions of a day and applicant’s reply is due on the corresponding day of the month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Reply to a 3-month period dated Nov 30 is due Feb 28 (or 29). A 1-month extension moves due date to the corresponding day of the next month. A 30-day period includes weekends/holidays but if it ends on a weekend/holiday the reply is timely if filed the next business day. The Office date stamp on the reply paper determines receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods: permitted lengths and prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Under authority of 35 U.S.C. 133, the Commissioner has directed the examiner to set a shortened period for reply to every action; the shortened period may be less than 6 months but not less than 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indication of a shortened time for reply should appear prominently on the first page of all copies of actions in which a shortened time for reply has been set so a person scanning the action can easily see it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of shortened statutory periods by situation (1-, 2-, 3-month rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specific shortened statutory periods: (1) 1 month — requirement for restriction/election only, or correction of inadvertent omission; (2) 2 months — winning party in terminated interference to reply to an unanswered action; Quayle (formal matters) actions; (3) 3 months — to reply to any Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These periods may be changed under special circumstances but generally apply as listed. See cited MPEP sections for each situation (e.g., §809.02, §714.14, §2173.05(n)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits (non-abandonment consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain examiner-specified time limits require an applicant to take a particular action within a set time and failure to timely take the specified action results in a consequence other than abandonment (e.g., disclaimer, decision rendered without applicant input).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Petition under 37 CFR 1.14(e) — usually 3 weeks to state objections to access petition; failure doesn't affect prosecution but Office decides without objections. (B) IDS incomplete — examiner may set 1-month time limit to complete IDS; failure results in noncompliant material being placed in file but not considered. (C) Allowable application with traverse of restriction — 1-month time to cancel nonelected claims or petition; failure treated as authorization to cancel and application passed to issue. Suggested claims for interference must be presented within not less than one month; failure is treated as a disclaimer, not abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between shortened statutory periods and specified time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified time for a particular action and a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 are distinct: the penalty for missing a specified time typically affects particular matter (e.g., disclaimer), while missing a statutory period results in abandonment of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 is not appealable, though petitions to revive may be available. A specified time limit can be less than 30 days and the examiner may excuse short delays at their discretion; a reply even a day late under a statutory shortened period results in abandonment (subject only to revive petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (petition+fee) and (b) (sufficient cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1) If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed, unless exceptions apply. (b) When paragraph (a) is not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; requests under (b) must be filed on or before the day reply is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition+fee under (a) extends time effective on filing of petition and payment and may be filed with or without the reply. Extensions cannot extend beyond statutory maxima. Requests under (b) must state reasons and are discretionary; filing alone does not grant the extension. See cross-referenced rules for specific proceedings (appeals, reexams, interferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods not extendable after Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, certain time periods are not extendable if set in the Notice or in an Office action with a mail date on or after the Notice: (1) period for submitting oath/declaration in compliance with § 1.63; (2) period for submitting formal drawings under § 1.85(c); (3) period for making a deposit under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These particular post-allowability periods cannot be extended by 37 CFR 1.136 if set in the Notice of Allowability or in a later-dated Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive petition and authorization to charge as extension (37 CFR 1.136(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request in an application may be an authorization to treat any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension under 1.136(a) as incorporating a petition for extension of time. An authorization to charge required fees or submission of the fee under § 1.17(a) will be treated as a constructive petition for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision acts as a 'safety net' when applicants inadvertently omit an explicit petition. The Office nonetheless strongly recommends including a written petition in reply to avoid processing delays; a sample one-sentence petition form is provided in the guidance. The date the petition and fee are filed determines the extension period and fee amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for extensions and small entity reduction; cumulativity and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for extensions of time are set in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are subject to a 50% reduction for small entities. The fees itemized are cumulative; additional extension months require payment of the appropriate incremental amount (subtracting previously paid amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions with fee cannot extend time beyond the statutory maximum (e.g., 6 months under 35 U.S.C. 133). Certain proceedings (reexamination, interference) and specific Office actions exclude availability of paid extensions. Applicants should carefully calculate the correct cumulative fee to obtain the desired length of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where extensions under 1.136(a) are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under 1.136(a) are not available in certain situations, including (A) all extensions in a reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.550(c)), (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding, (C) specific situations where an Office action states 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to a Notice of Allowability), and (D) instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When (a) is not available, (b) may be the only route (sufficient cause), subject to its filing timing and limitations. Cross-reference the applicable MPEP sections for each exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner treatment of bona fide but deficient replies
rubrics_metrics.description: When a bona fide attempt to reply includes an omission that does not preclude action on the merits (e.g., reply fails to address a rejection or objection), the examiner may waive the deficiency and act on the application, or issue an Office action that treats the reply on its merits and may also require supply of the omission to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omission precludes action on merits (unsigned amendment, missing fees), examiner may accept reply as adequate to avoid abandonment and give a shortened statutory 1-month period to correct. Examiner has discretion to determine whether omission was inadvertent or abusive; if abusive, the omission must be corrected within original reply period (including permitted extensions). Examiner may repeat and make final the rejection/objection that was the subject of the omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limit effect when failure may result in abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where failure to take the specified action may result in abandonment (e.g., filing a new complete appeal brief correcting deficiencies in a prior appeal brief), a time period should be set for taking the specified action and the action should specify whether provisions of 37 CFR 1.136 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a condition requires no extensions under 1.136, the Office should clearly indicate that 1.136 (or 1.136(a)) does not apply to the time period for taking action so applicants are aware extensions are not permitted.
